full_judgment: 6. It is true that the offence of "rioting" described in section 146 is not a minor offence in ABDUS SAMAD Vs. STATE (Shahabuddin Ahmed CJ) relation to an offence of murder under section 302, or culpable homicide (not amounting to murder under section 304 of the Penal Code. But 10 this case, the main charge against the accused-petitioners was that they were members of an unlawful assembly the common object of which unlawful assembly was to murder that labourer, Giasuddin. It was also found on evidence that in prosecution of this common object a murder was committed by some members of the unlawful assembly. The charge was, however, framed under section 302, read with section 34, instead of section 149. But judgment of the trial Court shows that accused Mojibor, Ahmed, Jatin and Abdus Samad were held guilty of the offence under section 304 Part II, read with section 149 of the Penal Code. In the order-portion of the judgment, however, two convictions were recorded separately one under section 304 (II) with the sentence of five years rigorous imprisonment and another under section 149, with the sentence of one year rigorous imprisonment. All the accused-petitioners had been further charged under sections 447/149, but they were acquitted there from. This anomaly appears to be due to the trial Court's misconception of the provisions of sections 141, 143, 146, 147, 148 and 149 of the Penal Code and the applicability of sections 34 and 149.
